title: Settings puts the kill switch first, then sign-ins and machines, then the session, with display preferences folded under Look and feel and Calm mode left in view
description: Settings in packages/web/src/settings/SettingsPage.tsx is a long run of equal groups: the kill switch, then Calm and rewards, Appearance and Keyboard, Policy and Session, with the site's machines and sign-ins in between. The things the Owner comes to Settings for are mixed with display preferences he sets once. Reorder it: the kill switch first; then sign-ins (Accounts and API keys) and Machines on the site; then the session (pairing on the Mac, the signed-in email on the site) with Sign out. After the session comes a Look and feel section. Calm mode stays in view there as its own switch (the Owner chose this, and probes/ui/rewards-calm reaches it without opening anything). Rewards with its two sub-toggles, Motion, Theme, Table density and the Keyboard settings (single-key shortcuts and how the kill switch asks) fold under one disclosure button named Look and feel, closed by default (aria-expanded false, its settings not rendered until opened). Policy stays as it is: locked and read-only. Every preference keeps working.
acceptance: Settings shows the kill switch first, then on the site Accounts and API keys and Machines, then Session, then Look and feel
Calm mode is in view without opening anything and turns calm on
A Look and feel button, closed by default, holds Rewards and its two sub-toggles, Motion, Theme, Table density and the Keyboard settings, none of them shown until it is opened
Opening Look and feel shows them all
Policy is still shown, locked and read-only, without opening anything
